Patagonia's scale is hard to grasp until you're actually driving through it, with hours of open steppe between towns and mountains that seem to grow larger the closer you get.

## Choosing a route

Most self-drive itineraries link Chile's Carretera Austral with Argentina's Ruta 40, crossing the border at least once depending on how much time you have.

## Vehicle and fuel planning

Gravel sections are common on the Carretera Austral, and fuel stops can be far apart, so a vehicle in good condition and a habit of topping off early matter more here than on most road trips.

## Weather and seasons

Patagonian weather shifts fast even in summer, and travelers should plan for wind, rain, and sun within the same afternoon regardless of the forecast.

The reward for the long driving days is scenery that rarely repeats — glaciers, fjords, and granite spires each dominate a different stretch of the route in turn.
